reference.quote: End the range when a bar closes above RH (upside breakout) or below RL (downside breakout).

draw.today: a horizontal dash floored at 0.6 bar widths -- about 1.3px at the default 15m zoom -- at the extreme that gave way, stamped on the bar that closed through it and labelled 'breakout' in the side's colour; all 41 events on this window answer bars: [t, t] and the 20-bar range whose edge broke is never drawn -- including the break at bar 50 whose consequences the other two rows in this cluster spend 450 bars describing
draw.canonical: the boundary first and the break on it: the range drawn as a zone between its high and its low across the bars that made it, running right until a close ends it, with the bar that closes beyond an edge marked at that edge

fires.our_rule: the newest close beyond the high (or below the low) of the 20 bars *before* it -- a Donchian channel computed on the prior 20 bars, so a break never includes its own bar in the boundary it breaks; direction from which edge gave way
fires.their_rule: a boundary the market had been respecting, defined in advance, cleared by a decisive close rather than a wick; the same page's own calculation sets RH = max(H) and RL = min(L) over a window of 'commonly around 20' bars and ends the range when a bar closes beyond either

reference.quote: Watch for the failure: price cannot hold beyond the level and closes back inside, often within a few bars.

draw.today: one dash at a single price, 80,451.18, re-stamped on the newest bar: the 50 events this window returns are 50 consecutive bars (451-500 of 501) at that one price with zero-width spans, and the break they refer to is bar 50 -- the level and both of its moments are drawn nowhere
draw.canonical: the level with its two moments on it -- the bar that closed beyond it and the bar that closed back inside -- drawn between them and labelled at the second, since the event is the re-entry that reclassifies the break, not the break

fires.our_rule: scan the window's channel breaks oldest first and take the first one with ANY later close back on the original side; the look-forward is unbounded (candles[i+1..] reaches the newest bar), so one break produces a Failed Breakout on every bar from the reclaim to the end -- bars 68 through 500 here, 433 of the 480 replayable -- and the loop then breaks, so no newer break is ever examined
fires.their_rule: a close beyond followed by a close back inside, 'often within a few bars' -- a two-bar sequence anchored on the re-entry bar, with the strictness an explicit choice the reference names (any poke that re-enters vs a close beyond then a close back)

rule_as_data.rule: first i in [20, n) with close[i] outside channel(i-20..i-1); emit if any close[j], j in (i, n], is back on the original side

reference.quote: A retest is a return to a level that price has already broken, approached now from the other side.

fires.our_rule: the first break in the window not yet reclaimed whose level a later bar wicked back to, with the newest close still on the breakout side -- so it holds on every bar from that touch to the reclaim (bars 51-67 here) instead of firing at the touch, and formed_at is None so each event lands on the newest bar
fires.their_rule: three ingredients -- a level, a confirmed break, and a return -- judged at the returning bar: 'rejection wicks and a close back in the breakout direction argue the level held', and the touch is read against a volatility-scaled zone because 'defense happens across a band of prices'

reference.source: LuxAlgo docs, Price Action Concepts: Market Structure
reference.quote: Swing points are displayed retrospectively, and as such are not detected where they are located.

draw.today: a dash at a swing high's (or swing low's) price stamped on today's bar and labelled 'higher_highs': 50 events across only 6 distinct levels, in runs of up to 13 consecutive bars, every one bars: [t, t]; the pivot is neither marked at its own bar nor joined to the previous swing, so the staircase the concept names is invisible
draw.canonical: the four-word swing vocabulary the reference itself prints -- HH, HL, LH, LL -- put at the pivot bar, retrospectively, so the word sits where the swing is and the trend reads from the positions of the words; a label floating at today's bar over a price from 100 bars ago is the opposite of that

fires.our_rule: collect every strict 3-bar swing high and swing low in the whole window, take the newest two of each, and fire when both pairs step the same way -- one event per bar while the pair holds, naming the newest swing's price; the loop pushes prices only, so the pivot's bar index is discarded inside the detector
fires.their_rule: a swing point is a label at a pivot, drawn retrospectively at the pivot's own bar, and its scale is a parameter the user sets (the toolkit exposes 5 for internal structure and 50-100 for swing structure, against our fixed 3)

rule_as_data.rule: |swings| >= 2 && (h2 > h1 && l2 > l1) -> Buy at h2 | (h2 < h1 && l2 < l1) -> Sell at l2, pivots strict over i-3..i+3

reference.quote: A horizontal zone bounded by a confirmed high and low that price rotates inside until a breakout ends it.

draw.today: a grey dash at the newest close -- direction neutral on all 50 events, so the slate colour, and price_level equal to evidence.close on all 50 -- zero-width, re-stamped on every bar the comparison holds (50 events in 15 runs, the longest 7 bars); the ten bars it is tight about are never drawn
draw.canonical: the box the tightening describes: a horizontal zone between the window's high and low that price rotates inside until a close beyond an edge ends it, read as a contraction by its shrinking height against the boxes before it -- the contraction is a property of that box, not a mark at today's close

fires.our_rule: the newest 10-bar high-low span is strictly less than the smallest of the ten preceding 10-bar spans, each offset one bar, recomputed against a sliding window; no direction, no zone, and the price it carries is the close, which is a bar, not a level
fires.their_rule: a range is at least two swing highs stopping in one zone and two swing lows in another, bounded RH = max(H) and RL = min(L) over ~20 bars, ended by a close beyond an edge; the sideways character is confirmed by 'heavily overlapping candles, alternating failures at both edges' rather than by a single span comparison

rule_as_data.rule: span(n) < min(span(n-2), span(n-3), ..., span(n-11)) where span(e) = max(high[e-10..e-1]) - min(low[e-10..e-1])

reference.quote: Draw the grid across the visible range and thin it when lines crowd the chart; levels with more trailing zeros stay, finer subdivisions go first.

draw.today: a dash at the figure -- all 27 events on this window name the same one, 80,000 -- zero-width, stamped on the crossing bar; and a one-bar box in the card, because the event carries the crossing bar's own wick as zone_low/zone_high while the grid step it actually used (magnitude 5,000) is read by neither renderer
draw.canonical: the grid drawn across the visible range before price reaches it: one named horizontal line per figure, running the whole window, thinned when the lines crowd and weighted by trailing zeros, with the reaction graded on it -- a crossing is an event on a standing level, never the level's only drawing

fires.our_rule: the previous close and the newest close straddle a line of the step 10^floor(log10(price)) / 2 -- 5,000 for BTC at 80,000, so the grid jumps an order of magnitude the moment price crosses 100,000 -- and direction comes from the close's own move; once per crossing, which still allows a run of 4 when price chatters across the line
fires.their_rule: nothing needs detecting: the trader chooses a grid density for the instrument and timeframe, keeps the figures with more trailing zeros, treats each as untested until price interacts with it, and then grades that reaction with the same rules as any other level

rule_as_data.rule: let step = 10^floor(log10(close)) / 2; ceil(min(close[t-1], close[t]) / step) * step > min && <= max

reference.quote: That is also why grading uses a zone rather than a line: defense happens across a band of prices, so a tolerance around the level, scaled to recent volatility, separates a wick probing the zone from a genuine failure.

fires.their_rule: a reaction at a level the market already respects, graded as rejection, absorption or acceptance through: a wick into the band whose close leaves it is the rejection, judged across the band rather than at an exact price

fires.their_rule: role reversal: the level price closed through and now holds from the other side, with the retest that holds as the observable proof -- the crossing is the event's first half, and this predicate never asks whether the level was ever on the other side

reference.quote: A trend regime label is a discrete classification stamped on each bar: uptrend, downtrend, or range, sometimes with strength grades.

draw.today: a zero-width dash at the newest close in the shift's colour -- 14 neutral, 9 bearish, 6 bullish across 29 events, every one bars: [t, t] and price_level equal to the bar's close -- labelled 'regime'; the state each shift announces has no drawing at all, so 29 shifts describe 30 stretches of the window and the chart receives 29 points, while the ADX reading that decided each one arrives as evidence.magnitude (41.41, 31.08, 25.18 in the sample) and is read by neither renderer
draw.canonical: the state as a full-height band across the bars that hold it, named with the regime's word and graded with the strength figure it was thresholded against -- a label stamped per bar is a band, not a scatter of points, and the shift is where the band changes colour, not an object of its own

fires.our_rule: classify the tail and the tail-minus-one and fire when they differ: ADX(14) above 25, the DI lines giving the side, and structure_lean (the same two-swing HH/LL test that pa.higher_highs reports) required to agree -- no dwell time and no hysteresis, which is why the window carries 29 shifts, one every ~17 bars
fires.their_rule: thresholded ADX with the DI lines for direction, then hysteresis or dwell time as a required step: 'require the new condition to hold for several bars, or use a stricter threshold to enter a state than to stay in it, so the label does not flip on every borderline bar'

rule_as_data.rule: classify(t) != classify(t-1), where classify = adx14 > 25 && (structure_lean == (plusDI >= minusDI ? Buy : Sell))
